title: Working with Categorical Hyperparameters
text: Many hyperparameter optimization scenarios involve categorical hyperparameters like optimizer type, activation function, kernel choice. spacefinder package handles fitting separate subspaces categorical level.

title: Working with Categorical Hyperparameters
text: benchmark_data includes three optimizers: SGD, Adam, RMSprop. Let’s explore differ:  Notice Adam tends achieve slightly higher performance SGD RMSprop.
code: # Performance by optimizer benchmark_data[, .(   mean_auc = mean(auc),   median_auc = median(auc),   sd_auc = sd(auc),   max_auc = max(auc),   n = .N ), by = optimizer] #>    optimizer  mean_auc median_auc    sd_auc   max_auc     n #>       <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> <int> #> 1:   RMSprop 0.7916034  0.9097144 0.1883038 0.9499907   301 #> 2:      Adam 0.8185814  0.9380809 0.1789091 0.9499937   399 #> 3:       SGD 0.8043445  0.9356146 0.1882794 0.9499810   300  # Visualize distributions ggplot(benchmark_data, aes(x = auc, fill = optimizer)) +   geom_density(alpha = 0.6) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "AUC Distribution by Optimizer",        x = "AUC", y = "Density") +   theme(legend.position = "top")

what: Creating a Task with Categorical Hyperparameters
title: Working with Categorical Hyperparameters
text: Include categorical hyperparameter task definition: * optimizer formula indicates separate subspaces fitted optimizer type.
code: # Explicit specification task <- TaskSubspace$new(   data = benchmark_data,   target_measure = "auc",   hps = c("learning_rate", "max_depth"),   cat_hps = "optimizer" )  # Formula interface and convenience function task <- as_task_subspace(   data = benchmark_data,   formula = auc ~ (learning_rate + max_depth) * optimizer )

title: Working with Categorical Hyperparameters
text: Train learner - automatically fit one subspace per optimizer:
code: learner <- LearnerSubspaceBox$new(task) learner$train(q_val = 0.9)

title: Beta Density Estimation
text: fitting subspace, can add probabilistic density information using augment(). fits Beta distributions hyperparameter dimension, allowing : Sample new configurations weighted toward better regions Estimate probability densities within subspace Understand parts promising Note: augment() available Box Polygon learners, Ellipsoid.

title: Beta Density Estimation
text: augment() function returns fitted Beta distribution parameters (α, β) hyperparameter.
code: # Train a box learner task <- TaskSubspace$new(   data = benchmark_data,   target_measure = "auc",   hps = c("learning_rate", "max_depth") )  learner <- LearnerSubspaceBox$new(task) learner$train(q_val = 0.9)  # Fit beta densities densities <- augment(learner) print(densities) #>        parameter    alpha      beta converged iterations #>           <char>    <num>     <num>    <lgcl>      <int> #> 1: learning_rate  25500.0  48560.83     FALSE          5 #> 2:     max_depth 307797.1 337230.58     FALSE          6

title: Beta Density Estimation
text: α = β = 1: Uniform distribution (values equally likely) α > 1, β > 1: Peak interior (preferred region) α > β: Peak toward 1 (prefers higher values [0,1]) α < β: Peak toward 0 (prefers lower values [0,1])
code: # Extract parameters for learning_rate lr_params <- densities[parameter == "learning_rate"] alpha <- lr_params$alpha beta <- lr_params$beta  cat("Learning rate Beta(", alpha, ", ", beta, ")\n", sep = "") #> Learning rate Beta(25500, 48560.83) cat("Mode at:", (alpha - 1) / (alpha + beta - 2), "\n") #> Mode at: 0.3443073

title: Beta Density Estimation
text: Higher density indicates regions good configurations concentrated.
code: # Plot beta densities x <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 200)  plot_data <- rbindlist(lapply(densities$parameter, function(hp) {   params <- densities[parameter == hp]   data.table(     parameter = hp,     x = x,     density = dbeta(x, params$alpha, params$beta)   ) }))  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = x, y = density)) +   geom_line(color = "#2E86AB", linewidth = 1) +   facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y") +   theme_minimal() +   labs(title = "Fitted Beta Densities",        subtitle = "Higher density = more promising region",        x = "Normalized position in subspace [0,1]",        y = "Density")

title: Beta Density Estimation
text: can sample fitted distributions generate new hyperparameter configurations: sampled configurations weighted toward promising regions.
code: set.seed(123) n_samples <- 5  # Get bounds bounds <- coef(learner) lr_bounds <- bounds[hyperparameter == "learning_rate"] depth_bounds <- bounds[hyperparameter == "max_depth"]  # Sample from beta distributions (in [0,1]) lr_params <- densities[parameter == "learning_rate"] depth_params <- densities[parameter == "max_depth"]  samples_unit <- data.table(   learning_rate_unit = rbeta(n_samples, lr_params$alpha, lr_params$beta),   max_depth_unit = rbeta(n_samples, depth_params$alpha, depth_params$beta) )  # Transform to original scale samples <- data.table(   learning_rate = samples_unit$learning_rate_unit *      (lr_bounds$max - lr_bounds$min) + lr_bounds$min,   max_depth = samples_unit$max_depth_unit *      (depth_bounds$max - depth_bounds$min) + depth_bounds$min )  print(samples) #>    learning_rate max_depth #>            <num>     <num> #> 1:   0.003049004  8.742565 #> 2:   0.003051527  8.730131 #> 3:   0.003066214  8.720304 #> 4:   0.003053779  8.722425 #> 5:   0.003054220  8.737221

title: Subspace learner base class — LearnerSubspace
text: Overview: Subspace learners identify promising regions hyperparameter space : Filtering configurations top quantile based performance measure Fitting geometric subspace (implementation-specific) filtered data Optionally allowing outliers via regularization parameter lambda Geometric Representations: learners represent subspaces via transformation \(y = Ax + b\) : \(x \[0,1]^p\) unit cube coordinates \(y \\mathbb{R}^p\) original hyperparameter coordinates \(\\mathbb{R}^{p \times p}\) defines shape orientation \(b \\mathbb{R}^p\) translation vector Different learner types impose different structure matrix \(\): Box: \(\) diagonal (axis-aligned hyperrectangle) Polygon: \(\) general positive definite (oriented hyperrectangle) Ellipsoid: \(\) general positive definite (full ellipsoid) Categorical Hyperparameters: task includes categorical hyperparameters, separate subspaces fitted categorical level independently. allows different geometries different categories (e.g., different learning rate ranges per optimizer). Regularization via Slack Variables: lambda parameter controls volume-outlier trade-: lambda = NULL: Hard constraints, points must fit inside lambda > 0: Soft constraints, allows outliers penalty Larger lambda: Smaller subspaces, outliers tolerated Smaller lambda: Larger subspaces, fewer outliers tolerated Workflow:

Train on top configurations learner$train(q_val = 0.9, lambda = 0.1)  # 4. Extract fitted parameters coef(learner, vectorize = TRUE)  # 5. Add density parameters augment(learner)

title: Axis-aligned hyperrectangle subspace learner — LearnerSubspaceBox
text: Learns axis-aligned hyperrectangles (boxes edges parallel coordinate axes) contain high-quality hyperparameter configurations.

title: Axis-aligned hyperrectangle subspace learner — LearnerSubspaceBox
text: Geometry: Fits hyperrectangle defined independent bounds per dimension: $$S = \{x \\mathbb{R}^p : l_i \leq x_i \leq u_i\}$$ transformation unit hypercube \(y = Ax + b\) : \(= \text{diag}(1/(u_i - l_i))\) diagonal (independent scaling) \(b = -l/(u - l)\) translation vector \(x \[l, u]\) points fitted subspace \(y \[0, 1]^p\) points unit hypercube Optimization (lambda specified): $$\min_{l,u,\xi} \frac{\lambda}{2}\|u-l\|_2^2 + \frac{1}{2n}\sum_t(\xi_t^- + \xi_t^+)$$ subject : \(l - \xi_t^- \leq x^{(t)} \leq u + \xi_t^+\), \(\xi_t^-, \xi_t^+ \geq 0\) Regularization parameter \(\lambda\) controls subspace size: larger values produce smaller subspaces outliers. Slack variables \(\xi_t^-, \xi_t^+\) allow configurations violate bounds. Uses ECOS solver. Special handling univariate case (\(p=1\)). Simple mode (lambda = NULL): Uses coordinate-wise min/max: \(l_i = \min_t x_i^{(t)}\), \(u_i = \max_t x_i^{(t)}\) outliers possible mode (hard constraints). Key Properties: interpretable: bounds directly specify valid ranges Fastest: O(np) diagonal matrices Best independent hyperparameters capture correlations hyperparameters Transformation matrix always diagonal Comparison learners: Box: Axis-aligned , fastest, interpretable Polygon: Can rotate (L-infinity norm), maintains sharp corners Ellipsoid: Can rotate (L2 norm), smooth boundaries, flexible

title: Ellipsoidal subspace learner — LearnerSubspaceEllipsoid
text: Learns minimum-volume ellipsoids contain high-quality hyperparameter configurations. flexible geometry smooth boundaries.

title: Ellipsoidal subspace learner — LearnerSubspaceEllipsoid
text: Geometry: Fits ellipsoid: \(E = \{x \\mathbb{R}^p : \|Ax + b\|_2 \leq 1\}\) Matrix \(\\mathbb{R}^{p \times p}\) positive definite. Center \(c = -^{-1}b\). Semi-axes determined eigenvalues \(^{-1}\). Optimization (lambda specified): $$\min_{\succeq 0, b, s} \lambda \cdot (-\log\det()) + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n s_t$$ subject : \(\|Ax^{(t)} + b\|_2 \leq 1 + s_t\), \(s_t \geq 0\) Uses SCS solver semidefinite programming. Volume minimization via \(-\log\det()\). L2 norm creates smooth ellipsoidal boundaries. Simple mode (lambda = NULL): Minimizes volume without slack variables. points must satisfy \(\|Ax^{(t)} + b\|_2 \leq 1\). Key Properties: flexible: arbitrary rotations scaling Smooth boundaries (corners) Optimal normally distributed data expensive: \(O(p^3)\) scaling \(p > 50\), consider Box Polygon learners Comparison learners: Box: Axis-aligned, rectangular, fastest Polygon: Can rotate, rectangular shape, intermediate cost Ellipsoid: Can rotate, smooth boundaries, flexible, slowest

text: Algorithm: categorical level (globally categorical hyperparameters): Extract fitted box bounds (min, max) hyperparameter Transform data unit cube: \(x = (y - min) / (max - min)\) Filter points coordinates lie \([0,1]^d\) Fit \(Beta(\alpha, \beta)\) dimension via weighted MLE Apply regularization requested: \(\alpha, \beta \geq 1\) valid points remain filtering (happen box learners lambda = NULL), returns uniform prior \(Beta(1,1)\) dimensions. Weights: Data points weighted performance (target measure values), normalized sum 1. gives influence higher-performing configurations fitting beta distributions. title: Augment oriented hyperrectangle learner with beta densities — augment.LearnerSubspacePolygon
text: Algorithm: categorical level (globally categorical hyperparameters): Transform data: \(z = ^{-1}(y - b)\) map \([-1, 1]^d\) Rescale unit cube: \(x = (z + 1) / 2\) map \([0, 1]^d\) Filter points coordinates lie \([0, 1]^d\) Fit \(Beta(\alpha, \beta)\) dimension via weighted MLE Apply regularization requested: \(\alpha, \beta \geq 1\) key difference Box learner oriented hyperrectangles use L-infinity norm \(\|z\|_\infty \leq 1\), defines hypercube transformed space \([-1, 1]^d\). rescale \([0, 1]^d\) fitting beta distributions. Matrix Inversion: Since \(\) general positive definite matrix (diagonal), uses Cholesky decomposition efficient stable inversion: \(^{-1} = (R^T R)^{-1} = R^{-1}R^{-T}\) \(R\) Cholesky factor. Weights: Data points weighted performance (target measure values), normalized sum 1. gives influence higher-performing configurations. Regularization: regularize = TRUE (default), ensures \(\alpha \geq 1\) \(\beta \geq 1\). prevents U-shaped densities ensures mode exists interior \([0,1]\). Categorical Hyperparameters: task includes categorical hyperparameters, separate beta distributions fitted combination hyperparameter categorical level.
